verdicts.reasoning: The items require students to break down a given number into its component parts, either by writing it as an addition expression representing the values of its digits or by modeling it with base-10 blocks.
All target numbers provided in the samples for the student to work with (e.g., 10, 20, 45, 50) are 2-digit numbers.

The text-based questions explicitly prompt the student to write the number as 'tens and ones' (using expanded form), and the interactive visual questions use base-10 blocks, which naturally model numbers using tens and ones.
